# Fitted GARCH(1,1) QuantLib oracle

`returns.bin` contains 50,000 IEEE 754 binary64 returns in little-endian order
(400,000 bytes). `oracle.json` records their SHA-256 digest, five values from
each end, the input recipe, and the fitted result. The binary is the input to
Rust and binding tests; readers can decode each eight-byte chunk as one `f64`.
It is tracked so tests do not need QuantLib or a platform-specific random-number
implementation.

The data and result come directly from QuantLib 1.43's C++ `Garch11`,
`MersenneTwisterUniformRng`, and `InverseCumulativeNormal`, following
`test-suite/garch.cpp::testCalibration` in QuantLib source commit
`9863b578af0caa4cecabf697196533e84a8308b6`. The process has alpha 0.2,
beta 0.3, long-term variance 0.4, seed 48, and zero initial return and
variance. Each return is an inverse-normal draw times the square root of the
process's forecast variance. Dates start on 1962-07-07 and advance one calendar
day per return. `Garch11(series)` fits with the default `BestOfTwo` mode.
`next_variance` is the square of the final volatility from
`fitted.calculate(series)`, the forecast for the day after the last return.

On macOS, regenerate or verify using the QuantLib 1.43 Python wheel and the
matching C++ headers (which identify themselves as `1.43-dev`):

```sh
uv run --with QuantLib==1.43 python crates/libitofin/tests/fixtures/garch_fit/generate.py --quantlib-include /path/to/QuantLib
uv run --with QuantLib==1.43 python crates/libitofin/tests/fixtures/garch_fit/generate.py --quantlib-include /path/to/QuantLib --check
```

The generator compiles `oracle.cpp` as a temporary C++ bundle and loads it
alongside the wheel's native library. It never calls libitofin. A local
`QuantLib` checkout at the repository root is the default include path;
`--quantlib-include` handles separate worktrees. Boost headers default to
`/opt/homebrew/include` and can be set with `--boost-include`. `--check`
compares regenerated bytes with both tracked files.

The four fitted values reproduce the upstream test's alpha 0.207592, beta
0.281979, omega 0.204647, and log likelihood -0.0217413 within its 1e-6
absolute tolerance. Use 1e-6 absolute tolerance for fitted values and next
variance in cross-implementation tests. The input bytes and digest should
match exactly when the tracked binary is consumed.
